articles.title: Cursor publishes "Agent Swarms and the New Model Economics" Primary source: cursor.com/blog/agent-swarm…
articles.summary: Cursor says it tested a two-agent setup by reimplementing the full 835-page SQLite manual in Rust from scratch with different model combinations. In its benchmark, Opus 4.8 as the planner plus Composer 2.5 as the worker reportedly achieved a 100% pass rate for $1,339, while GPT-5.5 doing both roles also hit 100% but cost $10,565. Cursor argues the key is splitting planning from implementation, which kept context from drifting and reduced merge conflicts from more than 70,000 to under 1,000. If accurate, the result suggests some coding tasks may be solved more cheaply by coordinating smaller role-specific models rather than using one expensive model for everything.
